metadata.title: Systematic review of Erasmus+ projects labelled as good practice and related to e-learning and ICT: Some case studies

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study is a systematic review of Erasmus+ projects using the Erasmus+ Project Results Platform (E+PRP) plus a questionnaire, semi-structured interviews, and focus groups. It does not use any ILSA micro-data (e.g., PISA/TALIS student or teacher achievement datasets) and therefore does not define or apply complex survey weights, plausible values, or replicate-weight variance estimation. The only “sampling” described is a multi-stage project selection and voluntary participation process (survey/interview/focus groups), not a probability sample of students/teachers from an ILSA framework. As a result, there are no ILSA weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to apply; any weighting would be inappropriate because the analysis is qualitative-to-quantified synthesis of project success factors rather than population-representative estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is not an ILSA/PISA/TALIS micro-data empirical analysis; it synthesizes Erasmus+ project information via document review, a coordinator questionnaire, interviews, and focus groups. Because there are no cognitive achievement outcomes with Plausible Values (PVs) and no PV-based scaling, PV handling is not applicable. Missing-data handling for PVs is therefore not relevant, and the paper does not report a missing-data protocol because the study’s core evidence base is project-level participation and qualitative categorization rather than statistical modeling of PV-based scores.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The study uses a multi-stage PRISMA-adapted process for Erasmus+ project review. First, it screens E+PRP projects for relevance to eLearning/e-Learning/ICT and restricts to Erasmus+ 2014–2020, eliminating 1549 projects (duplicates and non-2014–2020). Second, it applies inclusion criteria requiring eLearning/ICT connection, good practice labeling, KA1/KA2, and involvement of educational centers, eliminating 8509 projects that do not meet criteria. Third, it administers a questionnaire to project coordinators for projects meeting the criteria; only projects meeting additional requirements (educational centers involved; students and/or teachers involved; sustainability beyond funding) proceed to interviews, yielding 57 projects and 22 voluntary interview participants. Fourth, it selects 14 best-valued projects for focus groups based on quality evaluation and impact, with 13 participating in focus groups.

data.outcome_summary: This paper is a systematic review of Erasmus+ projects labeled as good practice and related to e-learning and/or ICT, using a PRISMA-adapted four-stage review process (project definition, selection definition, project selection, and analysis). Evidence is gathered from the Erasmus+ Project Results Platform (E+PRP), a coordinator questionnaire (21 items; ~15–20 minutes; sent Dec 2020–Jan 2021; responses collected until May 2021; response rate 22%), semi-structured interviews (Dec 2021–May 2022; 22 projects), and focus groups (July 2022; 13 projects). The results are synthesized as success factors and examples of project practices (e.g., needs-driven design, partner coordination, usefulness beyond funding, teacher/student participation, and ICT/eLearning integration), rather than as predictive modeling of student outcomes. No ILSA assessment cycle, grade/domain, plausible values, survey weights, or ML prediction metrics are reported, and the study does not train or evaluate machine learning models.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction contains many nulls because the manuscript is a systematic review of Erasmus+ project practices rather than an empirical large-scale assessment (ILSA) analysis. It does not use ILSA micro-data (e.g., PISA/TALIS student achievement or PVs), does not report country-level student samples, and does not fit predictive ML models with performance metrics. Therefore, fields required for ILSA ML studies (PV handling, missing-data strategy for PVs, survey weights, ML algorithms, and main_findings with dataset→target→metrics) are not applicable to this paper’s design.
